findings.evidence: Line 138 `have hCM : ∀ i j, CM (σ i) (σ j) = CM i j := fun i j => congrFun₂ hσ i j` is the only use of `hσ`; it feeds the `simpa only [Function.comp_apply, hCM]` at lines 144-150, which without it would land on `CM.submatrix σ σ i j` by `rfl`. In-repo precedent for the general shape: `TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/FiniteType/Basic.lean:201` `theorem submatrix {C : Type*} [Fintype C] (h : IsFiniteType A) {e : C → B} (he : Function.Injective e) : IsFiniteType (A.submatrix e e)`.
findings.fix: State `theorem IsSerreSystem.submatrix {B' : Type*} [DecidableEq B'] {f : B' → B} (hf : Function.Injective f) (h : IsSerreSystem R CM H E F) : IsSerreSystem R (CM.submatrix f f) (H ∘ f) (E ∘ f) (F ∘ f)` — the current proof body with `hCM` deleted, `lie_E_F_of_ne` using `hf` — and keep `perm h hσ := hσ ▸ h.submatrix σ.injective` as the one-line corollary. Nothing at the use sites changes: in `IsSerreSystem R CM ...` the matrix is a parameter, not a type index, so `hσ ▸` rewrites only the Prop and `serreDiagramHom`/`serreLift_comp_serreDiagramAut` still typecheck unchanged.
findings.issue: `IsSerreSystem.perm` assumes `CM.submatrix σ σ = CM` and restricts to `σ : Equiv.Perm B`, but the hypothesis is used only to rewrite the conclusion's matrix back to `CM`. The natural statement needs neither: any injective reindexing `f : B' → B` sends a Serre system for `CM` to one for `CM.submatrix f f`. As stated, a downstream comparison of presentations for `CM` and `CM.submatrix e e` (relabelled Dynkin diagrams, the Layer 9 isomorphism theorem) cannot reuse this lemma and must re-prove all seven fields.

summary: The Serre-system stability lemma `IsSerreSystem.perm` carries an invariance hypothesis that is used only to rewrite the conclusion, and is restricted to `Equiv.Perm B`; the hypothesis-free `submatrix` form is strictly more general with the same proof and matches the repo's own `IsFiniteType.submatrix`. Everything else (the `negSwap` symmetry, the matrix helper lemmas, the automorphism constructions and their group law) sits at the right level.
